originality.rationale: Detailed rare-seed first-hitting n^-2 expansion uses minimal k+1 disjoint-seed term plus k+2 triple and paired-intersection collision types. General OR dynamics and minimum Kneser total-domination literature do not imply these probability coefficients alone. Actual published-finding corpus searches found different k=2 NOR/XOR/majority claims and general minimum domination results; residual uncatalogued rare-hypergraph enumeration remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: A classical or uncatalogued rare-uniform-hypergraph transversal expansion could imply the same two-motif n^-2 coefficient.

value.rationale: The n^-2 coefficient separates two genuinely different minimal near-domination obstructions for a natural temporal basin statistic. Neither the Poisson leading tail nor the known minimum total-domination size determines it; the coefficient provides quantitative finite-size probabilities for sparse activation in an infinite natural disjointness-network family.
